notes.drag: carriage drag: none until a source gives one
notes.generation: 4: a 2000s missile (weapons.ibx's generation 4 = from 1995); keys only its weapons.ibx section
notes.kg: the article's weight; whether it includes the launch tube is open
notes.power: 250: below a fighter's 300, so one hit damages and two destroy (inferred: a 1.42 kg warhead against the AIM-9M's 9.4 kg)
notes.blast_m: the lethal radius is open; held by blast scaling (inferred): the AIM-9A / B's 9 m (ds-aim9) for its 4.5 kg warhead (docs/real-weapons.md §1.4) times the cube root of this warhead's mass ratio (1.42 kg)
notes.motion._absAcceleration: 120 m/s², the AIM-9M record's (inferred: no burn time published)
notes.motion._spiralAccelBeta: top speed a / beta: 120 / the top speed
notes.motion.burn: the burn with which the missile's launch zone from rest (combat.gd fires from the unit's pose at speed 0; missile.rs dlz with "burn": the distance travelled in burn + 4 s) is its published range
notes.motion._timeAcceleration: the burn, so the original's reading of the section flies as long
notes.motion._timeConstOrientation: flies straight 0.5 s after launch (the AIM-9M record's)
notes.motion._fireReleaseInterval: open: the reader's default 0.5 s (combat.gd); one missile in the air at a time (docs/ai.md §14)

footnotes.w-misagh: Wikipedia, "Misagh-2" (12.74 kg, 1.42 kg HE, 850 m/s, 6 km, 5 km, IR fire and forget) (read 2026-11-03), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misagh-2
footnotes.ds-aim9: designation-systems.net, "Raytheon AIM-9 Sidewinder" (AIM-9A / B effective kill radius about 9 m), https://www.designation-systems.net/dusrm/m-9.html
